definitions.explanation: A person appointed by a government to conduct diplomacy with foreign nations. Includes ambassadors, consuls, and other diplomatic staff.

examples.japanese: {彼女|かのじょ}は{外交官|がいこうかん}として{働|はたら}いている。
{外交官|がいこうかん}は{外交官|がいこうかん}{特権|とっけん}により{現地|げんち}の{法律|ほうりつ}から{免除|めんじょ}される。
examples.english: Diplomats are exempt from local laws through diplomatic immunity.

examples.japanese: {父|ちち}は{外交官|がいこうかん}だったので、{子供|こども}の{頃|ころ}は{世界中|せかいじゅう}を{転々|てんてん}としていた。
examples.english: Because my father was a diplomat, I moved around the world during my childhood.

notes:
USAGE: {外交官|がいこうかん} is a neutral, standard term for a diplomatic official. It covers all ranks of diplomatic personnel.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {外交官|がいこうかん}{特権|とっけん} (diplomatic privilege/immunity)
- {外交官|がいこうかん}を{目指|めざ}す (to aspire to become a diplomat)
- {外交官|がいこうかん}{試験|しけん} (diplomatic service examination)

SIMILAR WORDS: {大使|たいし} (ambassador) is a specific rank — the highest-ranking diplomat in a foreign country. {領事|りょうじ} (consul) handles citizen services and trade in cities outside the capital. {外交官|がいこうかん} is the general term encompassing all diplomatic staff.

cross_references.notes: Consulate — the office where consular diplomats work
